ordered_diagnoses: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction

s1.syndrome_frame: subacute febrile illness with back pain and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: fever and back pain lasting 3 weeks
key_facts: 76-year-old Japanese man
presented with fever and back pain
endoscopic treatment for common bile duct stones 3 weeks prior
medical history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension
taking cilnidipine and metformin hydrochloride
smoking 20 cigarettes per day for 47 years
consuming 70g of ethanol daily
elevated CRP (22.1 mg/dL) and WBC (11,910/μL)
low platelet count (10.3 × 104/μL)
elevated ALP (275 U/L) and low albumin (1.7 g/dL)
abnormal liver imaging with two hypodense lesions in the right liver lobe
multiple cavitated nodules in lungs on CT and MRI
thrombosis of hepatic vein on CT and MRI
low-density area of left-sided iliopsoas muscle swelling on CT and MRI
enlarged high-signal areas in L4/5 intervertebral disc on MRI
gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining
positive cultures (blood, urine, and abscess fluid) for identified organism

per_call: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction

shortlist: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction

shortlist.label: Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess
shortlist.why_kept: elevated CRP, WBC, and abnormal liver imaging with hypodense lesions, along with gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining and positive cultures

shortlist.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: thrombosis of hepatic vein on CT and MRI, and abnormal liver function tests

shortlist.label: Infective Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: fever, back pain, and elevated inflammatory markers, although no clear heart murmur or Osler's nodes

shortlist.label: Pott's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: back pain and abnormal imaging findings, including enlarged high-signal areas in L4/5 intervertebral disc on MRI

shortlist.label: Nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: subacute febrile illness, multiple organ involvement, and positive cultures, although the identified organism is not specified

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of endoscopic treatment for common bile duct stones, which is a risk factor for developing a liver abscess. The presence of fever, back pain, and elevated CRP and WBC count also support an infectious process. The imaging studies show two hypodense lesions in the right liver lobe, which is consistent with a liver abscess. Additionally, the Gram staining and cultures are positive for gram-negative bacilli, which is consistent with Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.

rejected.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis due to membranous obstruction
rejected.why: While the patient does have thrombosis of the hepatic vein, the presence of a liver abscess and positive cultures for gram-negative bacilli suggest an infectious process rather than a primary thrombotic event.

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of heart murmur, Osler's nodes, or Janeway lesions, which are common findings in infective endocarditis.

rejected.label: Pott's Disease
rejected.why: The patient does not have any symptoms or imaging findings consistent with spinal tuberculosis, such as muscle weakness or sensory impairments.

rejected.label: Nocardiosis
rejected.why: While Nocardia infection can cause abscesses, the Gram staining and cultures are positive for gram-negative bacilli, which is not consistent with Nocardia infection.
